input.cause: The texts the model read said to cite "the fact its signed rules bound it by" and "the fact's id as its reference". Nothing said the reference field takes one id and nothing else. The model (claude-sonnet-5-5) joined the bounding fact test.speedFloorPercent with a second, supporting fact (scrubber.effectiveFlowAtFull, scrubber.minimumSpeedElevated, habitat.co2.elevatedPpm), often with prose added. The guard (harness/core/justify.ts) accepts exactly one id as the reference, so it refused with "is not a fact of the library". That refusal was true: it named the signed fact and its side (test.speedFloorPercent = 30, at or above), and the model's first retry kept only that id. The same form recurs across many other tasks of the exp-control, exp-learn, exp3 and exp4 workshops. Since commit 287f5bc the one-id rule is stated in specs/procedure/words.json /brief/safetyBounds ("by its id alone as the reference") and in harness/core/justify.ts ("Exactly one: for library, one id as library.facts lists it"). The tasks of the lead did not read those statements. The gap is closed in the texts today.

input.summary: Diagnosis diag-d51a49a86fed accepted by the guard. Lead D2:8cba194716f8 is right: it is a contract-gap. At the tasks' time (commit 4e3458b), the safetyBounds text in specs/procedure/words.json did not say that exactly one fact id is allowed as the reference. The prediction on that text came back false, meaning none of the safetyBounds text held the "single fact … by its id alone" wording at task exp3-baseline/t-2026-09-29-0010. The safety card said to cite "the fact's id as its reference", and the model read that as allowing two ids joined, for example "test.speedFloorPercent; scrubber.effectiveFlowAtFull 1 m3/min (scrubber-1-datasheet)". The guard refused this at step 8 with "is not a fact of the library". The model then narrowed the reference to test.speedFloorPercent and replaced the value, and the next submission was accepted. The refusal's words say what to cite, so the correction was reachable only through the refusal. The cause no longer holds today: both specs/procedure/words.json#/brief/safetyBounds and harness/core/justify.ts now state the single-id rule, and both predictions on this came back true. test.speedFloorPercent = 30 percent is a signed fact of commissioning-test-safety. The competing hypothesis, that the model ignored a stated rule, is ruled out: the text it read did not state the rule.
